label: D1 after a1-S1-rewarded, larger after recent doubt, early in episode
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * (100 - ep_trial) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * (tv("prev_reward", -1) != 1) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * (tv("prev_reward", -2) != 1) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * (tv("prev_action", -1) == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * (tv("prev_state", -1) == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (1 - last_is("a1 S1 r")) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == -1) * (prev_reward == 1) * belief * (100 - ep_trial) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r")
explanation: Active only at D1, and essentially only when the previous trial was a1 -> S1 (common) and rewarded; zero at GO and D2. Its size is set by the history before that trial. It is largest (~1.7) when the a1-S1 reward follows a trial that was unrewarded (+0.44) or that reached S2 (+0.36), smaller when the reward two trials back was also missing (+0.21 more), and it shrinks over a run of consecutive a1-S1 rewards (roughly 1.75 -> 1.35 -> 0.95 -> 0.65). It is strongly reduced (-0.47) if the trial before was an a2 choice (i.e. right after switching to a1). Within a1-S1-r it also falls with episode trial, on top of the timing baseline. On the first trial of a window, where the previous choice is unknown, a rewarded D1 is fit by belief x (100 - ep_trial). All other D1 histories sit below the timing baseline. Ideal-observer belief adds little once trial history is in the model. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.52 (dev 0.52), above the 0.47 all-cue additive ceiling and well above the 0.29 all-observed ceiling. The earlier policy-based explanation (policy decile reference 0.22) is not needed: observed history alone gives no loss. Remaining error is mostly windows that start inside a reward run, where the run length cannot be seen.

issues: The scores reproduce. On the test split the 8 terms give R^2 beyond timing 0.517; timing alone gives 0.097. The feature is zero at GO and D2. At D1 the residual is +0.238 after a1 S1 r and between -0.08 and -0.09 after every other previous trial. The ep_trial term is real: dropping it lowers the score from 0.517 to 0.454 (weight 0.006 per trial, about -0.58 across the episode). The first-trial belief x (100 - ep_trial) term adds about 0.07 (0.451 without it, and 0.480 if a plain first-trial indicator replaces it).

One factual claim is wrong: 'peaks when the a1-S1 reward follows a trial that reached S2 (+0.36)'. The S2 effect only appears when that S2 trial was unrewarded. Splitting the S2 term by reward inside the full term set gives S2 unrewarded +0.445 and S2 rewarded -0.139. So after a1 S2 r -> a1 S1 r the feature is lower, not higher. A standalone table of the trial-before pattern within a1-S1-r D1s agrees (relative to a1 S1 r): a1 S1 u +0.10, a1 S2 r -0.24, a1 S2 u +0.75, a2 S2 r -0.31, a2 S2 u +0.26, a2 S1 r -0.22, a2 S1 u 0.00. The boost is therefore strongest after a rare-unrewarded trial (evidence that S1 is good) and is negative after trials that favour S2, rather than being an additive 'unrewarded' plus 'reached S2' effect.
The 'unrewarded trial before (+0.44)' claim is mostly true but blurred. With the S2 split, a1 S1 u before gives about +0.39, while a1 S2 u gives about +0.84.

The run-length decay (1.75 -> 1.35 -> 0.95 -> 0.65) is only partly captured. The terms see two trials back, so beyond the third trial in a run the model's prediction stops falling. An explicit run-length product of consecutive a1-S1-r trials scored worse (0.40), so this costs little.

There is no large systematic error class. In misses, the mean error by phase x previous trial is at most 0.015 (largest: D1 after a2 S1 r, +0.015). The worst windows are the first one or two trials of a window inside a reward run, where the history is unobservable, as the explanation itself says. The ideal-observer belief does not fix this: belief, belief_lo, belief_cover and belief*(1-belief) interactions on the first trial each add less than 0.001.

Belief adds little within a1-S1-r D1s: adding belief_lo terms leaves the history-free score at 0.175. This is consistent with 'belief adds little' once trial history is included. 'Loses nothing vs the policy' holds: 0.52 vs the policy-decile reference 0.22.
